findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass` in its body. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and (new in this PR) `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, none of which are implemented. Instantiating the class raises TypeError. The class is registered as the `detector_handler` of the `metric_alert_fire` GroupType, and `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of that type now raises inside `process_detectors` instead of being a no-op as before. The previous `evaluate` stub returned [] and worked. Either implement the abstract methods or keep this handler non-stateful. The TODO on line 10 ('This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction') is also now stale.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring says evaluate 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature and implementation now return a dict keyed by group key. Callers relying on the docstring would expect list semantics and the wrong container type.

findings.title: test_dedupe in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue expects an occurrence whose fingerprint does not match the evaluated group key
findings.body: The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]`. The test then calls `evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...)`, and the real code builds the occurrence with fingerprint `["<id>:group_key"]`. IssueOccurrence is a dataclass, so the `== expected_result` assertion compares unequal fingerprints and fails. The group key in the expected occurrence needs to be "group_key".

findings.title: Test helper ignores its `value` argument, so the hook's value propagation is untested
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it. Tests also pass unrelated values (6 in tests where the evaluated value is 100, 8, or 10), so the tests cannot catch a bug where the hook uses the wrong value to build the occurrence or event data. The helper should include the value in the occurrence (e.g. evidence or subtitle) and the tests should pass the actual evaluated value.

findings.title: Occurrences are produced to Kafka before detector state is committed
findings.body: `process_detectors` now calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` for every result (line 62) before `handler.commit_state_updates()` (line 68). Previously this path was effectively dead for stateful detectors, so this PR enables real production. If the state or dedupe commit fails after the Kafka produce succeeds, the dedupe value and state are not advanced. The same data packet is then reprocessed, the status is still OK or the old state, and a new occurrence with a new id is emitted again. Consider committing state first, or documenting and accepting at-least-once duplicate occurrences.
